title: Final: the journey of a byte
cards/0/q: The full path of a .NET program
cards/0/explain: Managed execution from start to finish.
cards/1/q: Build the CIL for return (a + b) * c;
cards/1/explain: Parentheses first: a + b means add. Then push c and multiply with mul.
cards/2/q: Hello.dll and a Native AOT build of hello were copied to a computer without .NET. What runs?
cards/2/explain: Native AOT is a standalone native file. Hello.dll needs the CLR, and there isn't one.
cards/3/q: Where is the method declared in this same assembly described?
cards/3/explain: MethodDef is for your own methods. MemberRef is for references to other code's.
cards/4/q: How many times does the JIT compile a method that was never called?
cards/4/explain: The JIT only works on demand. A method nobody calls stays a stub.
cards/5/q: What's inside a regular .NET assembly? Select all that apply.
cards/5/options/3: Machine code for every CPU at once
cards/5/explain: A regular assembly has no machine code: the JIT will produce it. No source code either.
cards/6/q: A public method in a C# library takes a uint. Someone wants to call it from a language without unsigned numbers. What would have warned you in advance?
cards/6/options/0: [assembly: CLSCompliant(true)]: the compiler would issue a warning
cards/6/options/1: The JIT on the first call
cards/6/options/3: Nothing, the CLR converts it on its own
cards/6/explain: The CLS is a set of rules for public APIs, and CLSCompliant turns on the check.
cards/7/explain: .NET 5+ uses ReadyToRun and Native AOT instead of NGen.
cards/8/explain: A cast is not a conversion. The CLR sees that o holds a number, not a string, and throws. o.ToString() would give you a string.
cards/8/wrong/1: That takes o.ToString(). A (string) cast only checks the type.
cards/10/q: Why does the same Hello.dll run on both x64 and ARM64?
cards/10/options/0: It contains CIL, and there's a JIT for each CPU
cards/10/options/1: It contains machine code for both
cards/10/explain: The big idea from lesson 1: CIL is shared, machine code is produced on the spot.
cards/11/q: Tiered JIT is on. A method has been called 5 times. What state is it in?
cards/11/options/0: Tier 0: it's nowhere near the "hot" threshold yet
cards/11/explain: Tier 0 appeared on the first call. Tier 1 comes after about 30 calls.
